lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Ahead of you, a sleeping village under a gray dawn. Two riders slip out past the last houses: a tall, thin knight on a bony horse, and me, on my donkey.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Softly, Sancho. Great deeds begin in silence, before the neighbors wake up and ask questions.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Before my wife wakes up, he means. No goodbyes, no note. Just saddlebags and a wine-skin and a lot of hope.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Ah, our new companion has joined us! I name you my second squire: Sancho is first, you are second, and in knighthood, ranks matter greatly.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Ranks. Friend, there are two of us. Second squire is also the last squire.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Every great order begins small. Forward, Rocinante! The world is full of wrongs, and not one of them knows we are coming.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Good, let's keep it that way. Stay beside me, friend; I packed for two, but I can share.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: We ride on through the fields; I'll call you when my master starts making promises.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: The sun climbs over the fields beside you. My master rides with his chin high, the way he does right before he promises something enormous.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Sancho, faithful squire. When I win a kingdom, and I will, I shall make you governor of an island.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: The island again. Friend, he's promised me this island all night, and I've never even seen one, so I'm not sure what you do with it.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: You rule it, Sancho. Wisely and well.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: So if I'm a governor, my wife would be... a queen?

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Naturally. And your children, princes.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Master, you've met my wife. She'd be a fine queen for one afternoon. Then she'd tell the whole court to wipe their boots.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Then a countess, perhaps. Leave it in God's hands.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: A countess. Hear that, friend? You're riding with royalty, future royalty, very far future.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: We'll ride a while in peace. I'll call you when I get hungry, which is soon.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: The road bends toward the plain of Montiel. Behind me the saddlebags bounce, and the wine-skin sloshes with every step my donkey takes.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Sancho. What is that sound?

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Breakfast, master. I brought bread, one small loaf, for emergencies.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Knights errant do not eat on the road. They live on glory.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Then you won't mind if I eat your half.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Eat, then. But your stomach will never be sung about in ballads.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: My stomach doesn't want a ballad, it wants bread. Friend, if we pass a bakery, say nothing, or he'll call it a castle and try to rescue it.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: The road runs on toward Montiel; I'll call you when the land opens wide.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: The fields fall away, and the plain of Montiel opens around you, flat and gold to the edge of the sky. The sun is up now, and heat shimmers off the road.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Do you feel it, Sancho? This is the very plain where my adventures were meant to begin.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: I feel the sun on the back of my neck. Is that the adventure?

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Hush. Somewhere out there, a wrong waits to be righted: a giant, a wicked knight, a dragon if we are lucky.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Or nothing. Flat ground is mostly nothing, master. That's why it's flat.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Nothing is only an adventure that has not arrived yet.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Friend, remember that one for his tombstone. Meanwhile I'm down to half a loaf, and I'm guarding it like a castle under siege.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: Stay beside me, friend. I'll call you when something shows up on the horizon.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Friend. Look at the ridge ahead of you. Thirty or forty windmills, tall as churches, their big wooden sails turning slowly against the sky.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Perfectly normal countryside. Except my master has just seen them.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Sancho.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Oh, no.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Do you see them?

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Giants.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Windmills.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Thirty giants! Maybe forty, maybe a thousand, I did not count, and every one with arms two leagues long!

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Master, those are sails. The wind turns them, and they grind flour for bread. You like bread.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Bread? Destiny stands on that ridge, and you speak to me of bread?

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: It is very good bread. Friend, that ridge is more bread than I have seen in my whole life.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Fortune is arranging our affairs better than we could have wished. This is righteous war, Sancho.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: So, he says giants, I say windmills. Friend, you have the deciding vote, and I know which way you're leaning.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: Stay close, friend. He's sizing them up; I'll call you when he picks one.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: The windmills are closer now. You can hear them creak, a long wooden groan, and each sail's shadow sweeps across the road like the hand of a clock.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Sancho. The one on the left.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: The windmill?

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: The giant. He has been watching us.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: He has no eyes.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Precisely... A professional.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Friend, are you still with me? Good. One of us should be.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Look! He waves his arms. He is challenging me.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: That's the wind, master.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: And why is the wind blowing?

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Because... huh. Actually, I don't know.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Ha! Even you admit there is a mystery.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: He won... he actually won one. Friend, never tell him; I need a bite of bread to recover.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: I have one more question for him; I'll call you before he does anything expensive.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Ahead of you the sails turn and turn. My master is polishing his lance with his sleeve, and that is never a good sign.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Master, before you attack. If you knock one down, who pays for the windmill?

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: The king.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Which king?

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: We will discuss that after the battle.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: And the flour? That mill grinds bread for half the valley. Knock it down and everyone eats soup.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Then the giant has stolen their bread, and I shall win it back for them.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Hm, that almost made sense. Friend, for half a second I agreed with him. Please don't let it happen again.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: He's gathering up his reins. Stay beside me, friend; I'll call you when he's ready.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: You are facing the windmills now. My master sits tall on Rocinante, his buckler braced on his arm, his lance in rest, pointed at the nearest sail.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: If you are afraid, Sancho, go aside and say your prayers, while I meet them in fierce and unequal combat.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: I'm not afraid, I'm right, and that's different. Friend, back me up here.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Do not flee, you cowards! It is one knight alone who comes against you.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Nobody is fleeing, master. They're bolted to the ground.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Lady Dulcinea, flower of beauty, I commend myself to you. Stand by me in this peril.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: He's talking to his lady. She's far away in Toboso, but he says she hears every word.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Friend, stay with me. Whatever those things are, we watch together. I'm holding the last of the bread, in case anyone needs comfort.

bridge.speaker: sancho
bridge.text: He's ready. Stay with me, friend; I'll call you the moment Rocinante moves.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Ahead of you, my master spurs Rocinante, and the old horse lowers his head and heads straight for the nearest windmill.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Rocinante breaks into a gallop. Ride with him if your legs feel good, or stay right here beside me. Either way, we see it together.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Wave all the arms you like, giant! For Dulcinea! You shall answer to me!

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Master, it's a windmill! It's a windmill!

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Just then the wind picks up. The great sail swings down, and the lance goes straight into it.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Crack. The lance shatters into pieces. The sail sweeps horse and rider up and drops them, rolling over and over across the plain.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: A worthy opponent...

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Hold on, master, I'm coming! Friend, come with me. That was the expensive part.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Dust settles around you. My master lies flat beside Rocinante, and I come bouncing up on my donkey.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: God help us, master. Didn't I tell you they were windmills? Nobody could miss it, unless he had windmills in his head.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Hush, friend Sancho. The sage Freston turned the giants into mills, to rob me of the glory of defeating them.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Of course. Freston. The enchanter nobody has ever seen.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: His arts will fail in the end. Help me up; we ride for Puerto Lapice, where adventures are thick on the road.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: And bread, I hope. Friend, from now on I only eat bread that was never a giant. Thank you for riding with us, second squire, go well.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Second squire, a knight is only as brave as the friend who rides beside him. I am glad it is you.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Friend, between you and me, this is the nicest part of the trip. Open road, good company, and nobody attacking anything.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Stay beside me, friend. Every road is better shared.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: That's the wisest thing he's said all week.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Still with us, friend? Good. My master talks to the sky, my donkey talks to nobody, so you're the best company on this road.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Heading home, friend? That's fine, good thinking even. The windmills aren't going anywhere.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: A wise squire knows when the day's road is done. Our quest will wait, exactly where we leave it.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: I'll save your place, and I'll save you some bread. Some of the bread. Come back whenever you like.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Farewell for now, second squire. Go in peace; our road will be here.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Previously, my second squire, we rode out of the village at dawn to right the wrongs of the world.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: And I came along on my donkey, with saddlebags, a wine-skin, and the promise of an island.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: No one saw us leave. Not one wrong in all the world suspects we are coming.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Not my wife, either. Friend, welcome back: the road is open, the bread is packed, and my master is already looking for trouble. Stay beside me.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Previously, on the plain of Montiel, we sighted thirty or forty giants on the horizon.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Windmills. He says giants, I say windmills, and they grind flour for bread.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Monstrous giants, with arms two leagues long. Fortune itself has placed them in my path, squire.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Fortune placed them on a ridge, where the wind is. Friend, welcome back: the windmills are right where we left them, still turning, and still not giants.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Previously, I faced the giants with my lance in rest, and commended myself to my lady Dulcinea.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: I told him they were windmills. He told me to go and pray if I was afraid.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: A squire's fear is natural. A knight's courage is not for sale.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Neither is my bread, and there is very little left. Friend, welcome back: he's still sitting on Rocinante, still pointing his lance at a windmill. Stay beside me.

scenes.title: The story, quickly, from the departure

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Here's the rest of the story, friend, told quickly. We ride out onto the plain of Montiel, and there on the ridge stand thirty or forty windmills.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Giants, Sancho! Monstrous giants! If you are afraid, go aside and pray.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: He commends himself to his lady Dulcinea, lowers his lance, and charges. The wind turns a sail, the lance shatters, and horse and rider roll across the plain.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: I rush to help him. Didn't I tell you they were windmills, master?

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: The sage Freston turned the giants into mills, to rob me of my glory. On to Puerto Lapice!

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: So we ride on, one lance lighter, and my bread is still safe. Thank you for riding with us, friend. Go well.

scenes.title: The story, quickly, from the windmills

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Here's how it ends, friend, told quickly. The windmills turn on the ridge, and my master is certain they are giants.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: If you are afraid, Sancho, go aside and say your prayers. I fight them alone.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: He commends himself to Dulcinea, braces his buckler, and charges on Rocinante. A sail catches the lance, it shatters, and horse and rider go rolling across the plain.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: I come running on my donkey to help him up. I did say windmills.

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: The enchanter Freston changed them into mills, to steal my glory. His tricks will fail. We ride for Puerto Lapice.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: And so we ride on, bruised but cheerful, with a little bread left. Thank you, second squire. Go well.

scenes.title: The story, quickly, from the charge

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: Here's how it ends, friend, told quickly. My master spurs Rocinante straight at the nearest windmill, shouting for Dulcinea.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: The wind swings a sail down. The lance shatters, and the sail flings horse and rider rolling across the plain.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: I come running on my donkey. Master, didn't I tell you they were windmills?

lines.speaker: quixote
lines.text: Hush, Sancho. The sage Freston turned those giants into mills, to rob me of my glory. But his arts will fail against my good sword.

lines.speaker: sancho
lines.text: So I help him up, and we ride on toward Puerto Lapice. He's sore, I'm hungry, and the bread survived. Thank you for riding with us, friend.
